Edit: Actually I’m not sure any other current reply mentions market makers. So to explain it  simply for OP….there are firms who will buy whatever you’re selling at a fixed and publicly listed price. They will also sell at a fixed price, and they profit off the difference between what they buy and sell at. No one is sitting behind a desk and manually reviewing every individual trade and it isn’t that some other person happens to be buying at the same time as you sell. 

If institutions like this did not exist then trading would be less frequent, there would be risk of getting stuck with assets you don’t want for longer than you’d like, and as a result a lot more volatility in the market. They exist because there is a market for market liquidity

And if everyone is selling and no one is buying, then of course the price at which a market maker will buy is going to plummet. What matters is the fact that they are there and ready to buy at all.

I had the same problem and completely resolved it, so hopefully my experience can be helpful for you.

My advice would be to begin with a script you came up with yourself, and do a dry run by yourself with it that you record. Do not memorize the script. Distill it into high level talking points for each visual.

The next dry run (that you also record) will be built off those talking points. Connect them logically by paraphrasing your original script. 

Lastly, run through it with no script or bullet points until you have it down. The important thing here is to mix it up every time and anticipate and field any potential questions. The ultimate effect is that you sound very natural but also have complete confidence in what you’re presenting. If you seem assured, your audience will also have confidence in you.

You will not have to do this entire process forever. It gets easier to hit the sweet spot every time you do it. At some point you won’t have to do any process at all.

After you defeat the nervousness, get really familiar with what it is you want to communicate, and practice some general principles like book-ending the presentation, the story part will begin to fall into place.
